staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the crash against this staged vulnerable checkout. The staged patch/fixed commit do not touch ext/ox/err.c, ext/ox/parse.c, or ext/ox/ox.c; they update workflow/example files only, so the vulnerability trace below is grounded solely in the vulnerable source plus the saved ASan reproduction.

classification.classification_note: The invalid read happens in `_ox_err_set_with_location()` when it dereferences a one-past-end pointer into a stack `ALLOCA_N` XML copy while computing line and column numbers for an unterminated text error.

bug_description.original: Dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow in _ox_err_set_with_location OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=470447384 ``` Crash type: Dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow READ 1 Crash state: _ox_err_set_with_location read_text read_element ```
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / default_crash_trace.txt / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The saved 360-byte witness reaches `Ox.parse()` with an XML-like payload whose first non-whitespace byte is `<`, so `ox_parse()` enters `read_element()` and later treats the child content as text. Along the crashing path, `read_text()` encounters no `<` before the copied NUL terminator, so `c = *pi->s++` reads that terminator and `set_error(..., pi->s)` is called after the post-increment has advanced `pi->s` one byte past the end of the stack `xml` buffer created by `to_gen()`. `_ox_err_set_with_location()` assumes `current` is still in-bounds and immediately evaluates `*current` in its backward scan loop, producing the reproduced `dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `ext/ox/err.c:37`. The staged patch artifact is unrelated to this code path, and Stage 01 did not save a fixed-build validation run.

source.description: First project-side consumption of the attacker-controlled Ruby string, deriving the copied byte count and source pointer that control the later stack allocation and one-past-end pointer.
source.value_from: The staged PoC is 360 bytes (`sample_info.json`), so `len` becomes 361 and `x` points at the same Ruby-string bytes that are copied into the parser buffer on the crashing path.
source.note: This is the scored source rather than the fuzzer entry point because it is the first project statement that reads the attacker-controlled input into vulnerability-relevant state used by the subsequent allocation, copy, and parser walk.

tainted_value_origin.description: Project-side read of the attacker-controlled Ruby string before it is copied into the mutable parser buffer.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The PoC bytes are first exposed to project code through `StringValuePtr(ruby_xml)` here, then copied unchanged into `xml` at step 3 because no BOM-related rewrite is evidenced on the crashing path.

root_cause.description: The error-location helper assumes `current` still points inside the XML buffer and dereferences `*current` before moving it backward or clamping it, so a caller-supplied one-past-end pointer is read out of bounds immediately.
root_cause.note: Step 8 passes `current = pi->s` after `read_text()` has already post-incremented past the copied NUL terminator, turning this first loop test into the actual invalid read.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The first evaluation of `*current` reads one byte past the stack `xml` buffer while formatting the parse error location.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `ext/ox/err.c:37`, with `read_text`, `read_element`, `ox_parse`, and `to_gen` immediately below it in the crashing stack.

parser_admitted.code: if ('<' != *pi.s) {  // all top level entities start with <
parser_admitted.description: After `next_non_white()` skips the witness's leading tab byte, the first non-whitespace byte is `<`, so the input is admitted to the top-level XML element path instead of failing the initial format check.

evidence_limitations: The staged `patch.diff` and metadata `fixed_commit` are unrelated to the crashing source files and do not express a source-level fix for this bug.
Stage 01 reproduced only the vulnerable build; `sample_state.json` records `patch_resolves: false` and there is no fixed-build dynamic validation artifact in this result directory.

coarse_trace.summary: The project first derives `len = 361` and the source pointer `x` from the attacker-controlled Ruby string, then chooses a stack `xml` buffer because `len <= SMALL_XML` and copies the witness plus its terminating NUL into it.
The parser state is initialized on that copied buffer, the first non-whitespace byte `<` admits the top-level element path, and the opened element reaches the child-content logic.

Because the next child byte is not `<`, the parser treats the remaining bytes as text. `read_text()` encounters no `<` before the copied NUL, post-increments `pi->s` while reading that terminator, and passes the resulting one-past-end pointer to `set_error()`.
The error formatter immediately dereferences the out-of-bounds `current` pointer in its backward line/column scan loop, matching the saved ASan dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow at line 37.

fine_trace.note: Source. `to_gen()` first consumes the attacker-controlled Ruby string to derive `len = 361` from the 360-byte witness and the source pointer `x` that will be copied into the parser buffer. Those two values govern both the destination extent and the bytes later scanned past the terminator.

Because `SMALL_XML` is 4096 and `len` is only 361, the false branch selects `xml = ALLOCA_N(char, len)`. That allocation choice puts the future out-of-bounds dereference on dynamic stack storage instead of heap storage.

The full witness plus terminating NUL is copied into the mutable stack `xml` buffer that the parser will destructively scan. The copied terminator is the exact byte later consumed by `read_text()` before the invalid pointer is passed onward.

The parser state is bound to the copied buffer. `pi.str` and `pi.s` start at the first byte of `xml`, while `pi.end` marks `xml + 360`, so the copied NUL from step 3 sits just beyond the declared content range at `xml[360]`.

After `next_non_white()` skips the witness's leading tab byte, `*pi.s` is `<`, so the initial format rejection is bypassed and execution continues into `read_element()` on the accepted top-level XML path.

The opened element is accepted as a non-empty element: `>` closes the start tag, `hasChildren` becomes 1, and `pi->s` advances to the first byte of the element body so the child-content loop will decide between nested markup and text.

In the child-content loop the next byte is not `<`, so the parser takes the text branch rather than any nested-element or closing-tag branch. `pi->s` is reset to the start of that text span and `read_text()` becomes responsible for finding the next `<` or the string terminator.

The text scan encounters no `<` before the copied NUL terminator. Because the code uses post-increment, reading that terminator advances `pi->s` from the terminator byte to one byte past the 361-byte stack allocation, and `set_error()` forwards that one-past-end pointer as `current`.

Sink and root cause. `current` arrives from step 8 already one byte past the stack `xml` buffer, but this loop tests `*current` before decrementing or clamping it back into range. That first dereference is the reproduced out-of-bounds read at `ext/ox/err.c:37`.

format.name: unterminated-xml-like-text
format.contract: The witness must present an XML-like document whose first non-whitespace byte is `<` so `ox_parse()` enters `read_element()`, then leave element text unterminated so that after the text branch starts, `read_text()` encounters no `<` before the copied NUL terminator and forwards `pi->s` after the post-increment into `_ox_err_set_with_location()`.
